interpretations.decision: An event is recorded only after D5 stages 1-17 pass: full S18 record validated by validate_context with id equality, record snapshot/generation equal to the leased active snapshot, artifact size and sha256 equal to the envelope, run_id re-derived from artifact/producer/snapshot independently of claims, results present in the record with (path, source_sha256) equal to the snapshot's indexed observations, outcome derived from atlas-junit-xml-profile.v1 equal to the claim; the event carries retrieval record id, run identity, artifact digest and snapshot ids; attestation operator_declared

Disagreement (derived != claimed), non-objective outcome (skipped, error, duplicate, mixed), absent selector, and missing provenance (no artifact, run or selector, or claims without --artifact) all reject the import as unverifiable_outcome with a closed detail; import is all-or-nothing, exit 1, empty stdout, output and store untouched; free text never verifies

Both commands only lease the graph read-only through open_active; nothing is written except --output by feedback-import (outside repo, repo/.atlas and graph root, atomic); feedback-rank writes nothing; inventories, db digests and table counts unchanged on success, rejection and usage paths

Opt-in only via --overlay atlas-feedback-ranking-policy.v1 with --store; each adjusted entry exposes adjustment{delta, rule, supporting_event_ids sorted}; failed outcomes recorded with scored false; annotations counted, never scored; policy_id printed

Event active only if every referenced (path, source_sha256) equals the queried snapshot's indexed observation AND (snapshot_id, generation_id) equals the queried pair; closed reasons path_not_indexed, source_fingerprint_mismatch, generation_mismatch in that precedence; every excluded event listed

Content-addressed event ids excluding operator labels and envelope order; dedup key (retrieval_record_id, artifact_sha256, selector); identical reimport merges to byte-identical store; differing bytes under one key reject conflicting_duplicate; sidecar bytes identical for identical store, snapshot and policy
Without --overlay the store is not read and the ranking is the identity permutation of the unchanged S18 context() result, equal to the MCP graph_query op=context bundle order for the same request

Compatibility with S22 means field names and the selector kind only: run_id, selector kind pytest_nodeid, snapshot_id and generation_id. The S35 run_id is sha256('atlas-test-run.v1:' + canonical JSON of the artifact profile, digest and size, the producer and the snapshot pair): a different domain from the S22 coverage_run_id, never a consumed or shared run identity, and no S22 artifact is read

NODEID path grammar [A-Za-z0-9_/-]{1,512} plus one trailing .py; store is self-consistent, not authenticated (LIMITATION 12, attestation operator_declared echoed per active event); truncated baselines are never rejected and the sidecar carries collection_stop (LIMITATION 13, disabled means no --overlay only); request validated through request_mode and context_limits.normalize with text required first; baseline position 0 pinned (policy pinned baseline_position_0); passed means no direct failure, error or skipped child; load_record also catches RecursionError and MemoryError; scoring matches bundle ids against the live baseline only (LIMITATION 3 says records are self-consistent, not replayed); held-out evaluation folds by retrieval record id; a changed annotation note is a conflicting_duplicate; a junit error is not objective; the memex root sits outside every inventoried tree and the saved record is the tool result structuredContent
feedback/ may also import atlas_aci.protocol.graph (request_mode and validate_context); atlas_aci.protocol.context is not imported directly because it must load after atlas_aci.protocol.graph
